title: AV1 OBU framing mismatch can bypass libheif coded-size limits
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: libheif stopped scanning at an unsized AV1 OBU while libaom continued to a later sequence header and frame, bypassing coded-size limits. An untrusted AVIF could trigger excessive memory allocation; the advisory reports about 884 MB for a 718-byte sample and says no memory corruption was observed.
ai_role: The item-level libheif advisory explicitly attributes discovery to Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-OSGR5L95. The release notes independently state that all listed security issues were found by the scanner. The Anthropic program sources establish model-based scanning, but no per-case model is identified.
classification_note: The primary advisory establishes a publicly disclosed security finding and direct Anthropic OSS Scanner attribution. No CVE had been assigned in the libheif release notes at the checked time; the distinct GHSA is used. No exploitation or zero-day status is asserted.
remediation_note: The final OBU is now explicitly sized before scanning and decoding so libheif and libaom see the same framing; fixed in libheif 1.23.7. The libheif v1.23.7 security release is dated 2026-10-26; deployed patch status is not checked.
